problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(7t)[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

A complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),$ where ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying the Form of a Particular Solution for Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs

Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $\mathbf{x}(t)=\mathbf{x}_c(t)+\mathbf{x}_p(t),$ where $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution $\mathbf{x}_p(t).$
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
\mathbf{x}(t)=\mathbf{x}_c(t)+\mathbf{x}_p(t)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_c(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/13785393b66b769c10efcbf7cf9f1bb4f05c412a1ddb8649427b659728c7bd3e.png)
of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e.
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/4b2dbbf0847dc9ea9f438e3848dca79da5f4e3f4473ab325a5f2c48e8b77e98c.png)
where $a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2$ are constants that are to be determined.

feedback.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{1}(t)+5\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\end{aligned}
$$

The systems of linear ODEs above can be written in matrix form as follows:

| ${x}^{′}(t)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  | $\,\,x(t)+\,\,$ |  | {{field-3}} |  |  | $\,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+\,\,$ |  | {{field-4}} |  | $\,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-5}} | {{field-6}} |  |  | {{field-7}} |  |  | {{field-8}} |  |  |  |  |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite our system, highlighting the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=3\cdot {x}_{1}(t)+0\cdot {x}_{2}(t)+5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=(-1)\cdot {x}_{1}(t)+2\cdot {x}_{2}(t)+1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in matrix form:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}].$
